reading: A small cross-shaped exemplar (centre colour, arm colour, optional diagonal colour) sits on the background; each single marker cell inside a large rectangle gets the exemplar stamped centred on it, and the exemplar's arms are then extended as full lines across that rectangle to its edges. The original exemplar is erased.
verb: stamp exemplar at markers and extend its arms

slots.unit: the multi-coloured exemplar component (centre cell + arms + diagonals), removed from its original place
slots.anchors: single odd-coloured cells lying inside the large rectangles
slots.extension: each arm direction present in the exemplar becomes a full line of the arm colour through the anchor, stopping at the rectangle's edge

why: every anchor gets the same exemplar centred on it; lines only in the directions the exemplar has arms; lines stay inside the anchor's rectangle

reading: The number N of 8-cells in the top row is a count; every colour that occurs exactly N times in the bottom data row gets a vertical bar of height N drawn directly above the grey separator, in the same columns as its occurrences.
verb: draw bars for colours with count N

slots.count: N = number of 8 cells in the top row
slots.selected colours: colours occurring exactly N times in the data row below the separator
slots.bars: for each occurrence column, cells in the N rows immediately above the separator get that colour

why: only colours whose frequency in the data row equals N are drawn; bar height equals N

reading: The single shape (h rows by w columns) is cut out and arranged in a four-armed pinwheel on a (2w+h)-square canvas: the original on the left, rotated 90 degrees clockwise on top, rotated 180 on the right, rotated 270 on the bottom, all facing an empty h-by-h centre.

slots.unit: bounding box of the only object
slots.placement: left arm = unit at rows w..w+h-1; top = rot90cw; right = rot180 (same as horizontal mirror here); bottom = rot270cw; centre h x h empty

why: output is 4-fold rotationally symmetric and its left arm equals the input shape's box

reading: Two horizontal and two vertical 8-lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels; the five panels of the plus pattern are filled by position: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1. Corner panels stay empty.

slots.panels: the 3x3 panels cut by the 8 separator lines

why: each non-corner panel is filled solidly with its position's colour

reading: The 3x3 input shows one shape in some colour; the output is a single cell whose colour names the shape (ignoring its colour): plus -> 6, X -> 2, the 'two-by-two block plus diagonal corner' shape -> 3, the '110/101/010' shape -> 1.

slots.pattern: binary mask of non-background cells of the 3x3 grid

why: same mask gives the same output colour on every pair, regardless of input colour

reading: Above a grey separator row is a block of mixed colours; the most frequent colour in that block is written into the centre cell of the bottom row.
verb: place majority colour at bottom centre

slots.source: cells above the grey separator row

why: only the bottom-centre cell changes, and it takes the majority colour of the top block

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a 9x9 output: block (i,j) is a copy of the input where input cell (i,j) has the input's most frequent colour, and empty (0) elsewhere.
why: every 3x3 block of the output is the input or all 0; a block holds the copy exactly where the input cell has the most common colour

reading: An empty grid gets a 3-coloured square spiral drawn from the top-left corner, running clockwise inward with a one-cell gap between successive turns.

slots.path: start at (0,0), go right along top row, down right column, left along bottom row, up left column to row 2, then turn inward keeping a 1-cell gap from the previous lap until no room remains

why: the output depends only on grid size; spiral cells are 3, gaps are 0

reading: A row has one coloured cell at each end; each colour is extended toward the other until the middle, where the single centre cell becomes grey 5.

slots.pair: the two end cells on the same row (left colour a, right colour b)
slots.fill: cells from left end up to just before the midpoint get a; cells from just after the midpoint to the right end get b
slots.midpoint: the centre cell between them becomes 5

why: each half of the gap takes its own end's colour; the exact midpoint is 5

reading: A two-coloured shape lies on one side of a blue separator line; it is reflected across the line with its original colours, while the shape left in place has its two colours swapped.
verb: reflect across separator and swap original's colours

slots.axis: the full blue (1) separator row or column
slots.subject: the single two-colour object
slots.mirror copy: reflection of the object across the axis, original colours
slots.original: stays in place with its two colours exchanged (a<->b)

why: the two sides are mirror images in shape; colours on the original side are the swap of the mirrored side
